subject: Logic
title: Bayes' Theorem
description: A fast breakdown of Bayes' Theorem for builders.

hook.text: A medical test is 99% accurate. You test positive. The chance you're actually sick? Way lower than 99%.

buildup.text: Bayes' theorem shows how to update the probability of a hypothesis when new evidence arrives.

discovery.text: It combines your prior belief with the evidence's strength to produce a posterior probability.

twist.text: If the disease is rare (1 in 10,000), even a 99% accurate test gives mostly false positives. Base rate matters.

climax.text: Bayes' theorem is now central to spam filters, medical diagnosis, AI, and courtroom evidence evaluation.

punchline.text: New evidence updates belief. It doesn't replace it.

quiz.question: What does Bayes' theorem calculate?
options: The probability of a test being accurate
The updated probability of a hypothesis given new evidence
The base rate of any disease
